awd_titl_txt: Conference: 2025 Summer Research Institute in Algebraic Geometry
awd_abstract_narration:
The 2025 Summer Research Institute in algebraic geometry is a large scale, three week long conference that will be held at Colorado State University in Fort Collins, Colorado, from July 14 to August 1, 2025. Plenary lecture series (accessible to the entire algebraic geometry community) will be scheduled during the mornings, and invited research seminars in the afternoons. Each week will explore several relatively focused themes, however the Summer Research Institute will stress the unity of the subject through smooth transitions from one theme to another. The proceedings of the Summer Research Institute will be published by the American Mathematical Society, and are expected to serve as a central reference source for algebraic geometers. This grant will support housing for 150 graduate students, postdocs and early career researchers in Colorado State University dormitories. The Institute is expected to play a pivotal role in the professional development of young researchers and influence their path for years to come.

The research themes covered by Institute activities include a wide cross-section of modern algebraic geometry: moduli of higher-dimensional varieties, birational geometry in positive and mixed characteristics and connections to commutative algebra, geometry of moduli, analytic methods in algebraic geometry, enumerative geometry, combinatorial aspects of algebraic geometry, hyperkähler varieties and derived categories, geometric aspects of Hodge theory, O-minimality and arithmetic aspects of Hodge theory, connections between algebraic geometry and topology, p-adic geometry, p-adic Hodge theory, and Shimura varieties, Varieties over global fields. The lectures will be delivered by top experts in each field with a reputation for excellent exposition. The Institute is expected to foster interactions and collaborations between experts from different areas of algebraic geometry. More information is available at https://sites.google.com/view/2025summerinstitute/home.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The 2025 Summer Research Institute (SRI) in Algebraic Geometry, held at Colorado State University from July 8 to August 1, 2025, represented the continuation of a prestigious tradition that occurs only once every ten years. Since its inception in 1954, this decennial gathering has served as the definitive forum for algebraic geometry—a branch of mathematics that studies the geometric properties of solutions to polynomial equations. This year’s Institute brought together almost a thousand of the world’s leading mathematicians, researchers, and students to synthesize the breakthroughs of the past decade and set the research agenda for the next.

The primary scientific outcome of the 2025 SRI was the comprehensive evaluation and advancement of the "state of the art" in algebraic geometry. The field has seen explosive growth in the last decade, particularly in areas like birational geometry, the study of moduli spaces (the "maps" of all possible geometric shapes), and the interplay between mathematics and theoretical physics.

Key intellectual themes  included advancements in Moduli Theory, Hodge Theory and Arithmetic Geometry and Combinatorial Algebraic Geometry, three important areas that combine both a rich history and fertile recent developments in the field of algebraic geometry. By hosting daily plenary talks by 21 world-renowned experts and dozens of specialized afternoon sessions, the Institute facilitated many new interactions and collaborations between researchers of different backgrounds, nationality,  and even different generations. These interactions are expected to lead to new research directions and publications. Keeping with tradition, the organizers will also edit the "Proceedings of the 2025 Summer Research Institute," a volume that historically becomes a foundational reference for the field for the following decade.
The 2025 SRI was designed with a heavy emphasis on the "Broader Impacts" of mathematical research, specifically focusing on dissemination, education, accessibility, and cross fertilization of the scientific community.
  • Training the Next Generation (The Bootcamp): A dedicated "Graduate Student Bootcamp" was held from July 8–12, immediately preceding the main conference. This intensive program provided nearly 200 graduate students and early-career researchers with the necessary background to engage with advanced plenary talks. This pedagogical foundation ensures that the next generation of scientists can participate in high-level research early in their careers.
    •
  • Broadening Participation: Through NSF funding, the organizers provided significant financial support to students, postdocs, and researchers from a wide variety of backgrounds. 
  • Global Accessibility: To ensure the benefits of the Institute reached those unable to travel to Colorado, all plenary sessions were streamed on Zoom and recorded and made available via a public YouTube channel. This digital archive serves as a permanent, free educational resource for students and researchers worldwide.
  • Community Building: By hosting the event at Colorado State University, the project also engaged the local academic community and fostered a spirit of international cooperation, with participants representing dozens of countries and institutions.
    •
Over the life of the award, the 2025 Summer Research Institute played an important role in unifying a fragmented and rapidly growing field. It provided a platform for veterans to mentor novices and for specialists to bridge different subfields. The outcomes include a renewed research roadmap for the decade, a trained cohort of young mathematicians, and a wealth of digital resources that will support mathematical education and discovery for years to come.
